newsitem.title: USA: Rivlin says economy strong, labor markets tight.
newsitem.headline: Rivlin says economy strong, labor markets tight.

text.p: Federal Reserve Vice Chair Alice Rivlin on Thursday said the U.S. economy seems uniformly strong across the country and that it is benefitting from tight labor markets.
In remarks to a business group, Rivlin also said that inflation is better behaved than had been expected, in part because of improvements in productivity.

"We seem to be in a period where almost everything is going well," she said, adding, "the strength of the U.S. economy is across industries, it is across regions...by and large this is an economy growing well across a very strong base."

She said that the U.S. was also seeing the benefits of tight labor markets "with companies dipping down further into the skill pool, we see training accelerating because it hard to get skilled workers, we see people taking advantage of the training."
She said this "does not look like an economy that is running out of steam or generating any obvious imbalances," adding the the very recent statistics confirm the continuing strength.
"As we move into 1997, everything looks much more consistant, the higher growth has continued, the statistics have converged, give or take some weather, on a picture of very strong momentum."

She said the the question for Federal Reserve policymakers is how to keep the expansion going at the highest sustainable rate. Rivlin said that while the Fed was uncertain what such a pace was, it clearly was not 3.5 or 4.0 percent.

"A little prudence and a bit of insurance has seemed to the Federal Open Market Committee a couple of weeks ago a good way to increase the likelihood that the good news continues for as long as possible," she said. "It's not sure how much insurance is needed, we at the Fed like everybody else are watching the signals as they come in."
